clue.text: Pleads with inspiring member of parliament to reveal bent members

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so one word takes the other inside it

parts.note: pleads means begs
a group of owls is called a parliament, so one member of it is an owl

explanation.surface: A lobbyist begs an MP to expose crooked colleagues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member of parliament' looks like an MP; it is an owl, from the collective noun 'a parliament of owls'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowlegs are legs curving outwards at the knee, so they are bent limbs.

clue.text: Speculate about angrier chaps' confusion

indicators.note: the word for speculate is wrapped about the other pieces

parts.note: to speculate is to gamble, or bet
wilder is a synonym of angrier, as in wild with rage
chaps are men

explanation.surface: A puzzled onlooker wonders why some men are so furious.
explanation.definitionFit: Bewilderment is a state of puzzlement, a close synonym of confusion.

clue.text: Reptile in zoo died, replaced by aardvark ultimately

indicators.note: one letter of the zoo gives way to another, signalled by this phrase

parts.note: Whipsnade is a large zoo in Bedfordshire, England

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of aardvark

explanation.surface: A reptile at the zoo has died and an aardvark has taken its place.
explanation.walkthrough: WHIPSNADE is an open-plan zoo north of London; its D is swapped for K, the last letter of aardvark.
explanation.definitionFit: A whip snake is a slender, fast-moving kind of serpent, so a reptile.

clue.text: No Trump may enter European country uncastrated

indicators.note: one piece going into another means it sits inside it

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland
NT is the bridge abbreviation for a no-trump contract

explanation.surface: A political jibe: Trump may be barred from visiting Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: NT is no trumps in the card game bridge, not the politician.
explanation.definitionFit: An entire horse is a stallion that has not been gelded, so entire means uncastrated.

clue.text: Inadequate soprano is unable to start to yodel

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for soprano in music
is unable means can't

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A poor soprano who cannot even begin to yodel.
explanation.definitionFit: Scanty is a plain synonym of insufficient, describing an amount too small to meet a need.

clue.text: Team being broadcast is not facing the front

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
a programme being broadcast is on, as in on air

explanation.surface: A sports team on television is being filmed from an odd angle.
explanation.definitionFit: Side-on means viewed or placed from the side rather than head-on.

clue.text: Important moment in match, when one might turn to jelly?

definitions.meaning: in tennis, a ... is the point that could win a set

definitions.text: when one might turn to jelly
definitions.meaning: a jelly sets at a certain point in cooling, its setting point

explanation.surface: A tennis player's legs turn to jelly at the crucial moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Set point is a tennis term for a decisive rally, and also read as the stage at which jelly solidifies.

clue.text: Police search boxing ring for fish

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, as if in a box

parts.note: a dragnet is a sweeping police search
O is shaped like a ring

explanation.surface: Police comb a boxing ring looking for a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxing ring' reads as one sport phrase; 'boxing' is the container signal and 'ring' is O.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragonet is a small, often brightly coloured bottom-dwelling sea fish.

clue.text: Work together to remove two layers of clothing in musical performance

indicators.text: to remove two layers of clothing
indicators.note: taking off outer layers strips two letters from each end of the word

parts.note: to work together is to cooperate

explanation.surface: Two people help each other strip off layers during a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: The two outer layers are CO at the front and TE at the back of COOPERATE.
explanation.definitionFit: An opera is a staged drama set to music, a kind of musical performance.

clue.text: Fritter reportedly might affect this?

indicators.note: reportedly means the word is heard rather than seen

parts.note: to fritter, as in fritter away, is to waste

explanation.surface: Eating a deep-fried fritter might well show on your midriff.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a verb, fritter gives waste; read as a fried snack, it might thicken the waist.
explanation.definitionFit: A fattening fried fritter is the kind of food that can expand the midriff.

clue.text: Insectivore's tense, enthralled by American cattle with heads in electric railings

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: being enthralled is being held captive, so tense is held inside

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: heads are the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A tense insectivore is captivated by American cows near electric fencing.
explanation.walkthrough: NEAT is an archaic word for cattle, as in neatsfoot oil.
explanation.definitionFit: The anteater feeds on ants and termites, making it an insect-eating mammal.

clue.text: Criminal excited by hot dancers

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A wrongdoer gets worked up watching sultry dancers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' looks like a link word but is part of the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Body snatchers illegally dug up corpses to sell to anatomists, so they were lawbreakers.

clue.text: Sailors to fake performance metric

indicators.note: to fake is to forge or fabricate, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Sailors are tempted to doctor their performance figures.
explanation.definitionFit: A loss ratio, such as claims against premiums in insurance, measures how a business is doing.

clue.text: Filling holes is game for children in part of New Zealand

indicators.note: a filling goes inside, here between the holes

parts.note: O is shaped like a hole, so two holes give two Os
tag is a playground chasing game

explanation.surface: Children play a hole-filling game somewhere in New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: Otago is a region in the south of New Zealand's South Island.

clue.text: Mother of Parisian sent back Dutch produce

indicators.note: something sent back goes the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
de is French for of, as a Parisian would say

explanation.surface: A Parisian mother returns some Dutch goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Edam is a round cheese made in the Netherlands, so a Dutch product.

clue.text: Don't provide enough support for carpet company, essentially, for final part of revival

indicators.note: one letter standing for another means it replaces it

parts.note: underlay is padding laid under a carpet

indicators.note: the final part of a word is its last letter
essentially points to the central letter of the word

explanation.surface: A carpet firm skimps on padding for the closing act of a revival show.
explanation.walkthrough: In UNDERLAY the L (end of revival) gives way to P, the middle letter of company.
explanation.definitionFit: To underpay is to give someone less than is owed, falling short in payment.

clue.text: Tired due to partying after photo-op, oddly

indicators.note: one piece comes after the other in the answer
oddly means take the odd-numbered letters
partying letters are let loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is worn out from celebrating after an odd photo opportunity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the anagram of DUE TO behind the odd letters; 'partying' is the anagram signal, not a description of the photo-op.
explanation.definitionFit: Pooped out is informal American slang for exhausted.

clue.text: Reclines in muddy sediment, which is most ridiculous

indicators.note: one piece sitting in another is placed inside it

parts.note: silt is fine muddy sediment
reclines means lies

explanation.surface: Wallowing in the mud is the daftest thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Silliest is the superlative of silly, meaning the most foolish or absurd.

clue.text: African film about swindle in Austria is boring

indicators.note: the film's title goes about, round, the swindle

parts.note: E.T. is the Spielberg film
gyp is a slang word for a swindle

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so it goes inside the word

parts.note: A is the international vehicle code for Austria

explanation.surface: A film about a con in Austria turns out to be dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is boring' reads as a film review, but it puts A into IN to give IAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An Egyptian comes from Egypt, a country in North Africa.

clue.text: Segment for organisation to describe current engagements

indicators.note: to describe can mean to draw round, so the anagram goes round the other piece
organising the letters means putting them in a new order

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A section of a firm must report on its present commitments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to describe' is used in the geometric sense of tracing round a shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Meetings are appointments or engagements in a diary.

clue.text: Benefit of metalloid with no resistance

indicators.note: with no means lacking the following piece

parts.note: boron is a metalloid element
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A chemistry note on the advantage of a frictionless semi-metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A boon is a blessing or advantage, a close synonym of benefit.

clue.text: Old personal assistant's becoming underworld boss

parts.note: Siri is Apple's voice-controlled personal assistant, here with its 's

explanation.surface: An elderly PA is promoted to lord of the dead.
explanation.walkthrough: The personal assistant is the digital one on an iPhone, not an office secretary.
explanation.definitionFit: Osiris is the Egyptian god who rules the land of the dead.

clue.text: About to leave oil production plant in glad rags

indicators.note: a piece that leaves is dropped from the word

parts.note: a refinery processes crude oil into fuels
re means about, as in business letters

explanation.surface: Someone quits their job at an oil refinery wearing their best clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad rags is slang for best clothes, exactly what finery means.

clue.text: Retiring televangelist exposes body part

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the letters are read backwards
exposes means the letters are shown inside the word

explanation.surface: A TV preacher stepping down reveals some flesh.
explanation.definitionFit: The navel, or belly button, is a part of the human body.

clue.text: Corrupt path very regressive

indicators.note: regressive means going backwards, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: a lane is a narrow path

explanation.surface: A politician's corrupt course is deeply backward.
explanation.definitionFit: Venal describes someone open to bribery, a plain synonym of corrupt.

clue.text: I slept with ten cooks, which is likely to lead to infectious disease

definitions.text: likely to lead to infectious disease

indicators.note: to cook is to tamper with, so the letters are altered

explanation.surface: Sharing a bed with ten chefs is a sure route to catching something.
explanation.definitionFit: Pestilent means tending to produce a deadly epidemic, from pestilence, a plague.

clue.text: Conclude Ireland is backward and second-rate

parts.note: to conclude is to infer

indicators.note: backward means the letters run in reverse

parts.note: ROI is short for Republic of Ireland

explanation.surface: Someone sneers that Ireland is behind the times and inferior.
explanation.definitionFit: Inferior means of lower quality, the same sense as second-rate.

clue.text: Before lunch, finally manage to go back in time

indicators.note: going back means the whole string is read in reverse
the letter comes before the next piece
finally points to the last letter of lunch

parts.note: to manage is to cope

explanation.surface: A busy person must manage a return trip before lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go back in time' reads as time travel, but 'go back' is the reversal and 'time' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is a long era or period, so a stretch of time.

clue.text: Protein excess seen regularly

parts.note: a glut is an oversupply or excess

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter

explanation.surface: A dietician spots too much protein in meals again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: Gluten is the protein in wheat and other grains.

clue.text: Dodgy lawyer restricted by flashy stereotype

indicators.note: restricted means confined within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A crooked lawyer is boxed in by a showy stereotype.
explanation.definitionFit: A shyster is slang for an unscrupulous professional, especially a lawyer.
